DAAD's official deadline list for the 2027/2028 intake of its Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS) sends you to each course's own website for the date. Each course runs its own selection.

posts.caption:

• You show £1,529 a month for courses in London, or £1,171 a month outside London, for up to 9 months.
• You also show your first year's course fees (up to 9 months), as on your CAS.
• The money must be held for at least 28 days in a row, and the end of that period must be within 31 days of the date you apply.

posts.title: Explainer: scholarship age limits, Chevening vs Türkiye Bursları
posts.caption:
"Am I too old for a scholarship?" Read the official rules before you give up on one, or before you spend weeks on one you can't get.

Two examples that work very differently:
• Chevening (UK): there is no upper age limit. What it asks for is at least two years (2,800 hours) of work experience. Work that was compulsory for your degree doesn't count.
• Türkiye Bursları (Turkey): bachelor's applicants must be under 21, master's under 30 and PhD under 35.

So a 34-year-old engineer can apply for Chevening, but is too old for a Türkiye Bursları master's.

Unofficial blogs often get these rules wrong, so always open the scheme's own eligibility page before you start.

Sources: chevening.org (eligibility and FAQs), turkiyeburslari.gov.tr

One more: some portals let you send the request before you submit the rest of the application. Do that early.

posts.title: Explainer: Chinese Government Scholarship, Type A or Type B
posts.from: group_post posted Chinese Government Scholarship 2026- CSC Scholarship 2026
posts.caption:
CSC 2027/28 applicants: before you fill in anything, decide your route.

• Type A (bilateral): apply through your home country's dispatching authority (in Pakistan, HEC). Beijing Normal University's page gives this window as November to April, with exact dates set each year.
• Type B (Chinese University Program): apply directly to a designated Chinese university, which recommends you to CSC; you choose Type B on the CSC form. Window: November to March.

A full award covers tuition, a dormitory or accommodation subsidy, a monthly stipend and comprehensive medical insurance. Flights are usually not included.

3. Never send passwords, OTP codes or bank PINs. No funder needs them.
4. Check the deadline and year yourself. Old posts get reshared every season with the dates unchanged.

Genuine schemes publish their calls on their own websites, and you apply there or through the university.

posts.title: Tip cards: emailing a potential PhD supervisor
posts.caption:
For MEXT applicants (especially research students and University Recommendation applicants): writing to a Japanese professor is often the first real step. What helps:

1. Read two of their recent papers and mention one by name, with one line on why it connects to your work.
2. Use a clear subject line: "Prospective PhD student: [your topic]".
3. Keep it to 150-200 words: who you are, why you fit their group, one clear question.
4. Attach a one-page CV. Send transcripts only if they ask.
5. Ask whether they are taking students for the next intake and how places are funded.
6. Follow up once after 1-2 weeks, then move on. Silence is normal and usually means a full inbox, not a judgement on you.

If a professor replies that they can't take you, thank them and ask if a colleague in the same field might. Many acceptances start that way.

posts.caption:

3. Check whether the university wants a VPD. It's uni-assist's certificate showing your grade converted to the German scale. You upload it to the university yourself. It stays valid for a year.
4. Only pay through uni-assist's own portal.

If your course starts in winter instead, the common uni-assist deadline is 15 July.
